neighbours.label: ' a' right after 'keep / keeps / kept' ('keeps a low profile', 'kept a diary', 'keeps a big dog'), where the kept thing follows; ' a' after other verbs (has, bought, wrote) stays quiet.
fire: The actor keeps a small flat in Rome.
My grandmother kept a diary for sixty years.
The minister keeps a low profile these days.
Sailors kept a careful watch at night.
She keeps a spare key under the mat.
He kept a record of every sale.
The farm keeps a few goats.
They kept a close eye on the weather.
quiet: The actor has a small flat in Rome.
My grandmother wrote a diary for sixty years.
The minister gave a short speech these days.
Sailors took a careful look at night.
She hides a spare key under the mat.
He made a record of every sale.
The farm sold a few goats.
They took a close look at the weather.

notes: Card: ' a' x4, ' kept' x3, ' he' x2, ' very' (Spektor ... keeps⟦ a⟧ low public profile; The bank ... kept⟦ a⟧ low profile); output (reversed) favours ' low', ' very', ' carefully'. Exploratory probe: 'keeps a low profile' 0.50, 'kept a low profile' 0.47, and 'keeps a big dog' 0.47 too, so the label is the verb 'keep', not the idiom.
